chunks: Say: 'Do you refuse to believe in Him who created the earth in two spans of time, and set up compeers to Him, the Lord of all the worlds?'
ai.seo_question: Who is the Creator of the earth mentioned in Surah Fussilat verse 9?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to discuss the duration of creation, with some scholars interpreting 'two days' (yawmayn) as two periods or epochs rather than literal 48-hour days, emphasizing God's sovereignty over time. It serves as a direct critique of the Meccan polytheists who attributed creation to lesser deities, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid (monotheism) as the foundation of faith. The phrase 'Lord of the Worlds' (Rabb al-Alamin) underscores God's comprehensive lordship over all realms, a key theme in Shia theological discourse on divine unity.
